name: @projexlight/sdk-secrets
summary: Tenant-scoped secrets store for ProjexCloud: holds the customer-supplied credentials each SDK needs to talk to external systems (Snowflake account keys, Salesforce OAuth refresh tokens, Twilio API keys, custom webhook signing secrets). Envelope-encrypted via sdk-vault, with versioned rotation + named references so application code never sees raw plaintext.

endpoints.description: Create or replace a named secret. Returns a stable ref (the plaintext is wrapped + discarded).
Read a secret by ref. Returns plaintext only to callers with secrets.read.<scope> permission.
Rotate a secret: write a new version + retire the previous after the consumers have switched.

events.name: secrets.secret.written.v1
events.description: Secret created or replaced; carries ref + version (NO plaintext).

events.name: secrets.secret.read.v1
events.description: Secret retrieved; carries ref, persona_id, caller_sdk for audit.

events.name: secrets.secret.rotated.v1
events.description: Rotation completed; carries old + new version numbers.

events.name: secrets.secret.retired.v1
events.description: Old version retired (no longer readable). Final compliance moment before key disposal.

models.description: Per-secret row: ref, current_version, scope (tenant_id / bu_id), purpose tag.
Per-version row: ciphertext, vault_key_id, created_at, retired_at, retired_reason.

hooks.name: putSecret
hooks.description: Create/replace a secret. Plaintext encrypted via sdk-vault; plaintext discarded from process memory.

hooks.name: getSecret
hooks.description: Retrieve a secret by ref. Audited; rate-limited per persona to surface anomalies.

hooks.name: rotateSecret
hooks.description: Write a new version + plan retirement of the old (with consumer-acknowledgement window).

hooks.name: startRetirementWorker
hooks.description: Background worker: retires versions past their grace window. Emits .retired.v1.

scenarios.title: Tenant uploads Snowflake service-user credentials
scenarios.when_to_use: Customer installs connector-snowflake; their Snowflake private key + service-user gets put into sdk-secrets so the connector can fetch it on demand.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Plaintext encrypted via sdk-vault, then discarded; ref returned. Emits .written.v1 (no plaintext).

scenarios.title: Connector fetches credential at sync time
scenarios.when_to_use: connector-snowflake's scheduled sync run pulls the credential just before opening the Snowflake session; never caches plaintext in app memory.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Plaintext returned (audited). Read event has caller_sdk + persona_id so anomalies show up in usage reviews.

scenarios.title: Tenant rotates Snowflake credentials after the security review
scenarios.when_to_use: Annual rotation. New private key uploaded; old key kept readable for grace window so any in-flight syncs finish, then retired.
scenarios.expected_outcome: New version written + emitted. Old version retires automatically after 24h; emits .retired.v1. Consumers read by ref get the new version on next fetch.

scenarios.title: Reactive: shred all secrets when tenant offboards
scenarios.when_to_use: tenant.offboarded.v1 → mark every (tenant) secret retired immediately + delete the wrapped ciphertext. Vault key shred via sdk-vault handles the cryptographic erasure.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Every secret marked retired; ciphertext deleted. .retired.v1 fires per row. Customer can prove cryptographic erasure to their regulator.

scenarios.title: Rate-limit catches anomalous read burst
scenarios.when_to_use: Defensive — if a persona suddenly reads 100 secrets in 60s, throttle + alert. May indicate a compromised service account or rogue tech.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Operator paged. Persona reads beyond the limit fail closed (rate-limit error). SOC2 anomaly-detection control satisfied.

compliance_posture.notes: Every read audited; reads outside business hours auto-flagged. PCI 3.5 + FedRAMP SC-13 key-management satisfied via sdk-vault envelope encryption. Cryptographic erasure on tenant offboard via vault-key shred — strongest GDPR Art-17 / Art-32 posture.
